title: Opening of Paradise Lost
text: Of Man's first disobedience, and the fruit / Of that forbidden tree whose mortal taste / Brought death into the World, and all our woe, / With loss of Eden, till one greater Man / Restore us, and regain the blissful seat.
translation_en: Of Man's first disobedience, and the fruit of that forbidden tree whose mortal taste brought death into the World, and all our woe, with loss of Eden, till one greater Man restore us, and regain the blissful seat.

title: Opening of A Tale of Two Cities
text: It was the best of times, it was the worst of times, it was the age of wisdom, it was the age of foolishness, it was the epoch of belief, it was the epoch of incredulity.
translation_en: It was the best of times, it was the worst of times, it was the age of wisdom, it was the age of foolishness, it was the epoch of belief, it was the epoch of incredulity.
source: Charles Dickens, A Tale of Two Cities

title: English Proverb Collection
text: A stitch in time saves nine. The early bird catches the worm. Actions speak louder than words. All that glitters is not gold. Better late than never.
translation_en: A stitch in time saves nine. The early bird catches the worm. Actions speak louder than words. All that glitters is not gold. Better late than never.

title: Opening of Don Quixote
text: En un lugar de la Mancha, de cuyo nombre no quiero acordarme, no ha mucho tiempo que vivía un hidalgo de los de lanza en astillero, adarga antigua, rocín flaco y galgo corredor.
translation_en: In a village of La Mancha, the name of which I have no desire to call to mind, there lived not long since one of those gentlemen that keep a lance in the lance-rack, an old buckler, a lean hack, and a greyhound for coursing.

title: Neruda - Poema 20
text: Puedo escribir los versos más tristes esta noche. Escribir, por ejemplo: La noche está estrellada, y tiritan, azules, los astros, a lo lejos.
translation_en: I can write the saddest verses tonight. Write, for example: The night is starry, and the blue stars shiver in the distance.
source: Pablo Neruda, Veinte poemas de amor

title: Spanish Proverbs
text: No hay mal que por bien no venga. Más vale tarde que nunca. Dime con quién andas y te diré quién eres. El que mucho abarca poco aprieta.
translation_en: Every cloud has a silver lining. Better late than never. Tell me who you walk with and I'll tell you who you are. He who grasps much holds little.

title: Opening of The Stranger
text: Aujourd'hui, maman est morte. Ou peut-être hier, je ne sais pas. J'ai reçu un télégramme de l'asile: «Mère décédée. Enterrement demain. Sentiments distingués.» Cela ne veut rien dire.
translation_en: Today, mother died. Or maybe yesterday, I don't know. I received a telegram from the home: "Mother deceased. Funeral tomorrow. Faithfully yours." That doesn't mean anything.

title: Baudelaire - L'Albatros
text: Souvent, pour s'amuser, les hommes d'équipage / Prennent des albatros, vastes oiseaux des mers, / Qui suivent, indolents compagnons de voyage, / Le navire glissant sur les gouffres amers.
translation_en: Often, to amuse themselves, the men of a crew catch albatrosses, vast sea birds, that follow, indolent companions of the voyage, the ship gliding over the bitter depths.
source: Charles Baudelaire, Les Fleurs du mal

title: French Proverbs
text: L'habit ne fait pas le moine. Petit à petit, l'oiseau fait son nid. Qui vivra verra. Il ne faut pas vendre la peau de l'ours avant de l'avoir tué.
translation_en: The habit does not make the monk. Little by little, the bird builds its nest. Who lives will see. Don't sell the bear's skin before you've killed it.

title: Opening of The Metamorphosis
text: Als Gregor Samsa eines Morgens aus unruhigen Träumen erwachte, fand er sich in seinem Bett zu einem ungeheueren Ungeziefer verwandelt.
translation_en: When Gregor Samsa awoke one morning from troubled dreams, he found himself transformed in his bed into a monstrous vermin.

title: Goethe - Erlkönig
text: Wer reitet so spät durch Nacht und Wind? Es ist der Vater mit seinem Kind; er hat den Knaben wohl in dem Arm, er fasst ihn sicher, er hält ihn warm.
translation_en: Who rides so late through night and wind? It is the father with his child; he holds the boy well in his arm, he clasps him securely, he keeps him warm.

title: German Proverbs
text: Übung macht den Meister. Morgenstund hat Gold im Mund. Wer zuletzt lacht, lacht am besten. Aller Anfang ist schwer.
translation_en: Practice makes perfect. The morning hour has gold in its mouth. He who laughs last, laughs best. Every beginning is hard.

title: Opening of The Divine Comedy
text: Nel mezzo del cammin di nostra vita / mi ritrovai per una selva oscura, / ché la diritta via era smarrita.
translation_en: In the middle of the journey of our life, I found myself within a dark forest, for the straight way was lost.

title: Opening of The Name of the Rose
text: Naturalmente, un manoscritto. Il 16 agosto 1968 mi fu messo fra le mani un libro dovuto alla penna di tale abate Vallet.
translation_en: Naturally, a manuscript. On August 16, 1968, I was handed a book written by a certain Abbot Vallet.
source: Umberto Eco, Il nome della rosa

title: Italian Proverbs
text: Chi dorme non piglia pesci. Tra il dire e il fare c'è di mezzo il mare. A caval donato non si guarda in bocca. Ogni lasciata è persa.
translation_en: He who sleeps catches no fish. Between saying and doing lies the sea. Don't look a gift horse in the mouth. Every opportunity left is lost.

title: Opening of The Lusiads
text: As armas e os Barões assinalados / Que da Ocidental praia Lusitana / Por mares nunca de antes navegados / Passaram ainda além da Taprobana.
translation_en: The arms and the heroes renowned, who from the Western Lusitanian shore, through seas never sailed before, passed even beyond Taprobana.

title: Opening of The Posthumous Memoirs of Brás Cubas
text: Algum tempo hesitei se devia abrir estas memórias pelo princípio ou pelo fim, isto é, se poria em primeiro lugar o meu nascimento ou a minha morte.
translation_en: For some time I hesitated whether to open these memoirs at the beginning or at the end, that is, whether to put my birth or my death first.
source: Machado de Assis, Memórias Póstumas de Brás Cubas

title: Portuguese Proverbs
text: Água mole em pedra dura, tanto bate até que fura. Quem não tem cão, caça com gato. De grão em grão, a galinha enche o papo.
translation_en: Soft water on hard stone, strikes until it bores through. He who has no dog, hunts with a cat. Grain by grain, the hen fills her crop.

title: Opening of Anna Karenina
text: Все счастливые семьи похожи друг на друга, каждая несчастливая семья несчастлива по-своему.
transliteration: Vse schastlivye sem'i pokhozhi drug na druga, kazhdaya neschastlivaya sem'ya neschastliva po-svoyemu.
translation_en: All happy families are alike; each unhappy family is unhappy in its own way.

title: Pushkin - I Loved You
text: Я вас любил: любовь ещё, быть может, / В душе моей угасла не совсем; / Но пусть она вас больше не тревожит; / Я не хочу печалить вас ничем.
transliteration: Ya vas lyubil: lyubov' yeshchyo, byt' mozhet, / V dushe moyey ugasla ne sovsem; / No pust' ona vas bol'she ne trevozhit; / Ya ne khochu pechalit' vas nichem.
translation_en: I loved you: love yet, perhaps, in my soul has not quite died away; but let it trouble you no longer; I do not wish to sadden you in any way.

title: Russian Proverbs
text: Тише едешь — дальше будешь. Без труда не выловишь и рыбку из пруда. Век живи — век учись.
transliteration: Tishe yedesh' — dal'she budesh'. Bez truda ne vylovish' i rybku iz pruda. Vek zhivi — vek uchis'.
translation_en: The quieter you go, the further you'll get. Without labor you won't pull a fish from a pond. Live a century — learn a century.

title: Opening of the Quran - Al-Fatiha
text: بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَنِ الرَّحِيمِ ﴿١﴾ الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ ﴿٢﴾ الرَّحْمَنِ الرَّحِيمِ ﴿٣﴾ مَالِكِ يَوْمِ الدِّينِ ﴿٤﴾
transliteration: Bismi-llāhi r-raḥmāni r-raḥīm. Al-ḥamdu li-llāhi rabbi l-ʿālamīn. Ar-raḥmāni r-raḥīm. Māliki yawmi d-dīn.
translation_en: In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Praise be to God, Lord of all the worlds. The Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Master of the Day of Judgment.

title: The Mu'allaqat - Imru' al-Qais
text: قِفا نَبكِ مِن ذِكرى حَبيبٍ وَمَنزِلِ / بِسِقطِ اللِّوى بَينَ الدَّخولِ فَحَومَلِ
transliteration: Qifā nabki min dhikrā ḥabībin wa-manzili / bi-siqṭi l-liwā bayna d-dakhūli fa-ḥawmali
translation_en: Stop, let us weep at the remembrance of a beloved and a dwelling place / at the edge of the sand dune between al-Dakhūl and Ḥawmal.

title: Arabic Proverbs
text: اللي ما يعرف الصقر يشويه. الصبر مفتاح الفرج. من جدّ وجد ومن زرع حصد.
transliteration: Illi mā yaʿrif aṣ-ṣaqr yishwīh. Aṣ-ṣabr miftāḥ al-faraj. Man jadda wajada wa-man zaraʿa ḥaṣad.
translation_en: He who doesn't know the falcon grills it. Patience is the key to relief. He who strives finds, and he who sows reaps.

title: Opening of"Dream of the Red Chamber
text: 满纸荒唐言，一把辛酸泪。都云作者痴，谁解其中味？
transliteration: Mǎn zhǐ huāngtáng yán, yī bǎ xīnsuān lèi. Dōu yún zuòzhě chī, shuí jiě qí zhōng wèi?
translation_en: Full of absurd words on every page, a handful of bitter tears. All say the author is mad, who can understand its flavor?
source: Cao Xueqin, Dream of the Red Chamber

title: Opening of"A Madman's Diary
text: 今天晚上，很好的月光。我不見他，已是三十多年；今天見了，精神分外爽快。
transliteration: Jīntiān wǎnshang, hěn hǎo de yuèguāng. Wǒ bù jiàn tā, yǐ shì sānshí duō nián; jīntiān jiàn le, jīngshén fènwài shuǎngkuài.
translation_en: Tonight, very good moonlight. I haven't seen him for over thirty years; today when I saw him, my spirits felt especially refreshed.

title: Chinese Proverbs
text: 学而不思则罔，思而不学则殆。三人行必有我师焉。千里之行始于足下。
transliteration: Xué ér bù sī zé wǎng, sī ér bù xué zé dài. Sān rén xíng bì yǒu wǒ shī yān. Qiān lǐ zhī xíng shǐ yú zú xià.
translation_en: To study without thinking is futile; to think without studying is dangerous. Among three people walking, there must be one who can teach me. A journey of a thousand miles begins with a single step.

title: Opening of Godan
text: होरी ने दोनों बैलों को, जो पहले से द्वार पर खड़े पागुर कर रहे थे, गाड़ी में जोता और एक घड़ा पानी लेकर खेत की ओर चला।
transliteration: Horī ne donõ bailõ ko, jo pahle se dvār par khaṛe pāgur kar rahe the, gāṛī mẽ jotā aur ek ghaṛā pānī lekar khet kī or calā.
translation_en: Hori yoked both bullocks, which had been standing at the door chewing cud, to the cart, and carrying a pitcher of water, headed toward the field.

title: Kabir Doha
text: बुरा जो देखन मैं चला, बुरा न मिलिया कोय। जो मन खोजा आपना, मुझसे बुरा न कोय।
transliteration: Burā jo dekhan main calā, burā na miliyā koy. Jo man khojā āpnā, mujhse burā na koy.
translation_en: When I went out looking for evil, I found none. When I searched my own mind, I found none worse than myself.

title: Hindi Proverbs
text: जैसा देश वैसा भेष। जहाँ चाह वहाँ राह। बंदर क्या जाने अदरक का स्वाद।
transliteration: Jaisā deś vaisā bheṣ. Jahā̃ cāh vahā̃ rāh. Bandar kyā jāne adrak kā svād.
translation_en: When in Rome, do as the Romans do. Where there is a will, there is a way. What does a monkey know of the taste of ginger?

title: Opening of The Tale of Genji
text: いづれの御時にか、女御、更衣あまたさぶらひたまひけるなかに、いとやむごとなき際にはあらぬが、すぐれて時めきたまふありけり。
transliteration: Izure no ohon-toki ni ka, nyōgo, kōi amata saburaitamaikeru naka ni, ito yamgotonaki kiwa ni wa aranu ga, sugurete tokimekitamau arikeri.
translation_en: In a certain reign there was a lady not of the first rank whom the emperor loved more than any of the others.
source: Murasaki Shikibu, The Tale of Genji

title: Matsuo Bashō - Haiku
text: 古池や蛙飛び込む水の音。閑さや岩にしみ入る蝉の声。夏草や兵どもが夢の跡。
transliteration: Furuike ya / kawazu tobikomu / mizu no oto. Shizukasa ya / iwa ni shimiiru / semi no koe. Natsukusa ya / tsuwamono-domo ga / yume no ato.
translation_en: An old pond — a frog jumps in, sound of water. Silence — seeping into the rocks, the cicada's cry. Summer grass — where warriors once dreamed.

title: Japanese Proverbs
text: 七転び八起き。猿も木から落ちる。石の上にも三年。出る杭は打たれる。
transliteration: Nana korobi ya oki. Saru mo ki kara ochiru. Ishi no ue ni mo san nen. Deru kui wa utareru.
translation_en: Fall seven times, stand up eight. Even monkeys fall from trees. Three years on a stone (patience). The nail that sticks out gets hammered down.

title: Opening of The Vegetarian
text: 아내가 채식주의자가 되기 전까지만 해도, 나는 그녀가 특별한 사람이라고 생각한 적이 없었다.
transliteration: Anaega chaesikjuuijaga doegi jeonkkajiman haedo, naneun geunyeoga teukbyeolhan sarami-rago saenggakhan jeogi eopseotda.
translation_en: Before my wife turned vegetarian, I had always thought of her as completely unremarkable in every way.

title: Yun Dong-ju - Counting the Stars
text: 죽는 날까지 하늘을 우러러 한 점 부끄러움이 없기를, 잎새에 이는 바람에도 나는 괴로워했다.
transliteration: Jungneun nalkkaji haneureul ureoreo han jeom bukkeureoumeul eopgireul, ipsaee ineun baramedo naneun goerowohaetda.
translation_en: Until the day I die, let me gaze up at the sky with not a speck of shame. Even the wind in the leaves tormented me.
source: Yun Dong-ju, Counting the Stars at Night

title: Korean Proverbs
text: 낮말은 새가 듣고 밤말은 쥐가 듣는다. 콩 심은 데 콩 나고, 팥 심은 데 팥 난다. 세 살 버릇 여든까지 간다.
transliteration: Nanmareun saega deutgo bammareun jwiga deunneunda. Kong simeun de kong nago, pat simeun de pat nanda. Se sal beoreut yeodeunkkaji ganda.
translation_en: Birds hear the words spoken in the day, mice hear the words spoken at night. Plant beans and you get beans, plant red beans and you get red beans. Habits formed at three last until eighty.

title: Opening of My Name is Red
text: Şimdi ben bir ölüyüm, bir ceset, bir kuyunun dibinde. Son nefesimi çoktan verdim, kalbim durdu.
translation_en: I am nothing but a corpse now, a body at the bottom of a well. I took my last breath ages ago, my heart stopped.
source: Orhan Pamuk, My Name Is Red

title: Nazim Hikmet - On Living
text: Yaşamak şakaya gelmez, büyük bir ciddiyetle yaşayacaksın, bir sincap gibi mesela, yani, yaşamanın dışında ve ötesinde hiçbir şey beklemeden.
translation_en: Living is no laughing matter: you must live with great seriousness, like a squirrel, for example — I mean without looking for something beyond and above living.

title: Turkish Proverbs
text: Damlaya damlaya göl olur. Bir elin nesi var, iki elin sesi var. Sakla samanı gelir zamanı. Aç tavuk kendini buğday ambarında sanır.
translation_en: Drop by drop, a lake forms. One hand has nothing, two hands have a voice. Save the straw, its time will come. A hungry chicken dreams it's in a wheat barn.

title: Swahili Proverb Collection
text: Haraka haraka haina baraka. Asiyefunzwa na mamaye hufunzwa na ulimwengu. Penye nia pana njia. Kidole kimoja hakivunji chawa.
translation_en: Hurry hurry has no blessing. He who is not taught by his mother is taught by the world. Where there is a will, there is a way. A single finger cannot crush a louse.

title: Shaaban Robert - Poem
text: Titi la mama litamu, lijapoacha na utamu. Lisilo na mama lina, mwana hulia machozi.
translation_en: The breast of one's mother is sweet; even when it dries, the sweetness remains. Without a mother, the child cries tears.

title: Opening of Siku Njema
text: Siku hiyo nilikuwa nimefurahi sana. Siku hiyo ilikuwa siku njema kwangu, siku ambayo sitaisahau kamwe.
translation_en: That day I was very happy. That day was a good day for me, a day that I will never forget.

title: Cavafy - Ithaca
text: Σα βγεις στον πηγαιμό για την Ιθάκη, / να εύχεσαι νάναι μακρύς ο δρόμος, / γεμάτος περιπέτειες, γεμάτος γνώσεις.
transliteration: Sa vgeis ston pigaimó gia tin Itháki, na éfchesai nánai makrýs o drómos, gemátos peripéteies, gemátos gnóseis.
translation_en: As you set out for Ithaca, hope the voyage is a long one, full of adventure, full of discovery.

title: Opening of Zorba the Greek
text: Πρώτη φορά τον είδα στον Πειραιά. Είχα κατεβεί στο λιμάνι ν'αποχαιρετίσω μιαν φίλη που ταξίδευε για τη Κρήτη.
transliteration: Próti forá ton eída ston Peiraiá. Eícha kateveí sto limáni n'apochairetíso mian fíli pou taxídeve gia ti Kríti.
translation_en: I first met him at Piraeus. I had gone down to the port to say goodbye to a friend who was traveling to Crete.

title: Greek Proverbs
text: Σιγά σιγά και το αυγό μαδάει. Όποιος βιάζεται σκοντάφτει. Τα πολλά λόγια είναι φτώχεια.
transliteration: Sigá sigá kai to avgó madáei. Ópoios viázetai skontáftei. Ta pollá lógia eínai ftócheia.
translation_en: Slowly, slowly, even the egg loses its feathers. He who hurries stumbles. Too many words are poverty.

title: Opening of the Aeneid
text: Arma virumque cano, Troiae qui primus ab oris / Italiam, fato profugus, Laviniaque venit / litora, multum ille et terris iactatus et alto.
translation_en: I sing of arms and the man, who first from the shores of Troy, exiled by fate, came to Italy and the Lavinian shores — much buffeted on land and on the deep.

title: Opening of the Vulgate Bible - Genesis
text: In principio creavit Deus caelum et terram. Terra autem erat inanis et vacua, et tenebrae erant super faciem abyssi, et spiritus Dei ferebatur super aquas.
translation_en: In the beginning God created heaven and earth. And the earth was without form, and void, and darkness was upon the face of the deep, and the Spirit of God moved upon the waters.

title: Opening of the Iliad
text: Μῆνιν ἄειδε, θεά, Πηληϊάδεω Ἀχιλῆος / οὐλομένην, ἣ μυρί' Ἀχαιοῖς ἄλγε' ἔθηκε.
transliteration: Mēnin áeide, theá, Pēlēïádeō Achilēos / ouloménēn, hḕ murí' Achaioĩs álge' éthēke.
translation_en: Sing, O goddess, the anger of Achilles, son of Peleus, that brought countless ills upon the Achaeans.

title: Opening of the Rigveda
text: अग्निमीळे पुरोहितं यज्ञस्य देवमृत्विजम् । होतारं रत्नधातमम् ॥
transliteration: Agnim īḷe purohitaṃ yajñasya devam ṛtvijam. Hotāraṃ ratnadhātamam.
translation_en: I praise Agni, the chosen priest, god, minister of sacrifice, the hotar, lavisher of wealth.

title: Opening of Beowulf
text: Hwæt! We Gardena in geardagum, / þeodcyninga, þrym gefrunon, / hu ða æþelingas ellen fremedon.
translation_en: Lo! We have heard of the glory of the Spear-Danes, of the kings of the people, in the days of old, how the princes performed courageous deeds.

title: Hávamál - Words of the High One
text: Deyr fé, deyja frændr, deyr sjalfr it sama; en orðstírr deyr aldregi hveim er sér góðan getr.
translation_en: Cattle die, kinsmen die, you yourself die likewise; but the fame of the one who has earned good repute will never die.

title: Lord's Prayer in Gothic
text: Atta unsar þu in himinam, weihnai namo þein. Qimai þiudinassus þeins. Wairþai wilja þeins, swe in himina jah ana airþai.
translation_en: Our Father, who art in heaven, hallowed be thy name. Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done, on earth as it is in heaven.

title: Hymn to Inanna
text: nin me šár-ra an ki-a diğir zi u₃-tud-da nú-me-a
translation_en: Lady of all the divine powers, resplendent light, righteous woman clothed in radiance, beloved of Heaven and Earth.

title: Code of Hammurabi - Prologue
text: inūma Anum ṣīrum šar Anunnakī Enlil bēl šamê u erṣetim šā'im šīmat māt nišī Mardukim māršu rēštiam ša Ea ellūtam ina teništim ušarši'ūšum
translation_en: When the august god Anu, king of the Anunnaki, and the god Enlil, lord of heaven and earth, who determines the destinies of the land, allotted supreme power over all peoples to Marduk.

title: Pangur Bán
text: Messe ocus Pangur Bán, cechtar nathar fria shaindán: bíth a menma-sam fri seilgg, mu menma céin im shaíncheirdd.
translation_en: Me and Pangur Bán, each of us at his special art: his mind is set on hunting, my mind on my special craft.

title: Opening of the Dao De Jing
text: 道可道，非常道。名可名，非常名。無名天地之始。有名萬物之母。
transliteration: Dào kě dào, fēi cháng dào. Míng kě míng, fēi cháng míng. Wú míng tiāndì zhī shǐ. Yǒu míng wànwù zhī mǔ.
translation_en: The Dao that can be told is not the eternal Dao. The name that can be named is not the eternal name. The nameless is the beginning of heaven and earth. The named is the mother of the ten thousand things.
